overview: Sweden is the largest country in northern Europe, on the Scandinavian peninsula. Its capital and largest city is Stockholm, which is built on a group of islands. Sweden is a constitutional monarchy. It joined the European Union in 1995 and, after two centuries of staying out of military alliances, joined NATO in 2024.

geography.text: Forests cover around two-thirds of Sweden, and it has close to a hundred thousand lakes. The north, reaching beyond the Arctic Circle, is mountainous and thinly populated, while the south is flatter and has most of the farmland and cities. Its long Baltic coastline is fringed with thousands of islands.

history.text: Swedish Vikings travelled east along the rivers of Russia. Sweden broke away from its union with Denmark in 1523 and became a great power in the 1600s, ruling much of the Baltic coast. It lost Finland to Russia in 1809 and has not fought a war since 1814. In the 1900s it built a famous welfare state.

events.title: Gustav Vasa
events.text: Sweden leaves the union with Denmark under its own king.

events.title: Gustavus Adolphus dies
events.text: Sweden's warrior king is killed at Lützen in the Thirty Years' War.

events.title: Last war
events.text: A short campaign against Norway is Sweden's last war.

events.title: First Nobel Prizes
events.text: The prizes founded by Alfred Nobel are awarded for the first time.

government.text: Sweden is a constitutional monarchy. The King is head of state but has no political power. The Riksdag, its parliament, chooses the Prime Minister. Sweden joined the European Union in 1995 but kept its own currency, the krona, and after two centuries of neutrality it joined NATO in 2024.

economy.text: Sweden has a high-tech, export-driven economy and a large welfare state. Famous Swedish companies include IKEA, Volvo, Ericsson, H&M and Spotify. Forests, iron ore and hydropower are important natural resources.

culture.text: Sweden gave the world ABBA, Astrid Lindgren's Pippi Longstocking and the game Minecraft, made in Stockholm. The Nobel Prizes, founded by Alfred Nobel, are awarded in Stockholm every December. Swedes celebrate midsummer by dancing around a maypole.

items.title: Pippi Longstocking
items.text: Astrid Lindgren's super-strong girl first appeared in 1945.

items.title: Fika
items.text: A coffee break with something sweet, a daily habit.

sport.text: Football, ice hockey and skiing are the most popular sports. Sweden has won the ice hockey world championship many times, and its tennis stars include Björn Borg, who won Wimbledon five times in a row. Pole vaulter Armand Duplantis has broken the world record again and again.

items.title: Björn Borg
items.text: Won Wimbledon five years in a row, 1976–80.

items.title: Armand 'Mondo' Duplantis
items.text: Olympic pole vault champion and world record holder.

didYouKnow: Sweden has an 'Ice Hotel' rebuilt from river ice every winter.
Sweden recycles so much waste that it has imported rubbish from other countries to burn for energy.

keyPeople.name: Alfred Nobel
keyPeople.text: Invented dynamite and founded the Nobel Prizes.

keyPeople.name: Greta Thunberg
keyPeople.text: Started school strikes for the climate in 2018.
